margin_over_naive_baseline.margin_on_a.reason: Mean per-benchmark reductions versus naive A are 33.982024% in CNOT count and 29.855811% in depth, with improvements on every benchmark. substantial_margin requires both metrics to reach 30%, whereas modest_margin specifies 10–30% CNOT/depth reductions. The metrics occupy different bands, and the rubric supplies no mixed-metric aggregation rule. Adjudication is needed to determine whether the limiting metric selects the tier or both must fall inside its stated interval.

margin_over_naive_baseline.margin_on_b.reason: Mean per-benchmark reductions versus naive B are 33.843386% in CNOT count and 21.282434% in depth, with improvements on every benchmark. The rubric does not specify how to combine these different bands; adjudication is needed before selecting a tier.

originality_and_literature.contribution_.reason: The work meaningfully extends hardware-cost-aware adaptive selection to real-time McLachlan dynamics through sufficient-set lexicographic selection and evaluates that extension against routing controls. Its novelty is limited by existing cost-aware adaptive methods and standard routing primitives, with ablations showing that most savings arise from topology-independent single-qubit preference.

originality_and_literature.literature_en.reason: The paper discusses more than eight relevant works across routing, compilation and variational dynamics, including SABRE, tket, Qiskit, Paulihedral, TETRIS compilation, ADAPT-VQE, AVQDS(T), Co-ADAPT-VQE and connectivity-restricted pools. It explicitly contrasts their objectives and algorithmic choices with this method.

originality_and_literature.spec_independ.reason: The paper has a self-contained scientific thesis and conventional article organization, but retains task-specific terminology and framing, including Topologies A/B, the smart-embedding naive baseline, the accuracy floor and explicit protocol-compliance language.
